entry.title: Remove `inline*` from `margin-trim` features
entry.content:
Summary

Remove "web-features:margin-trim" from the non-standard inline features as these were recently removed from the spec:
w3c/csswg-drafts#14284

MDN already reflects these being removed. However web-feature is still picking these up due to the tag and incorrectly showing a lack of support in browsers that support all the features: https://github.com/web-platform-dx/web-features/blob/main/features/margin-trim.yml.dist

The individual properties are not listed in web-features so they are picking up all BCD keys with this feature, including these non-standard ones. So we should remove the web-feature tag.

Test results and supporting details

The only browser that supported these was Safari and it is removing support from 27.3:

  • https://bugs.webkit.org/show_bug.cgi?id=322106
  • https://developer.apple.com/documentation/safari-release-notes/safari-27_3-release-notes#:~:text=Fixed%3A%20Removed%20the%20inline%2C%20inline%2Dstart%2C%20and%20inline%2Dend%20values%20from%20margin%2Dtrim%2C%20which%20now%20accepts%20none%20%7C%20block%20%7C%20%5B%20block%2Dstart%20%7C%7C%20block%2Dend%20%5D.%20(185527437)

entry.title: html.elements.option.label - clean up firefox notes
entry.content:
Summary

two of the three firefox notes on html.elements.option.label aren't really about the label attribute:

  • the note about keyboard/mouse events not bubbling from <option> to <select> is already on html.elements.select, so i removed the copy here.
  • the note about styling <option> belongs on html.elements.option, so i moved it there and updated it. it said styling was "still disabled in linux" while bug 1338283 was open. that bug is closed, but dom.forms.select.customstyling is still false on gtk (linux), and since bug 1703866 (firefox 102) it's also false on macos. when the pref is off, SelectParent.sys.mjs doesn't apply page color/background-color to the dropdown items. i set firefox_android explicitly so the desktop-only note doesn't get mirrored.

the "before 77" note on label stays since it is about the attribute.

Test results and supporting details

  • pref defaults are in modules/libpref/init/all.js in mozilla-central (#if defined(MOZ_WIDGET_GTK) || defined(XP_MACOSX) → false)
  • npm run lint and the pre-push checks pass

Related issues

fixes part of #12592 (points 1 and 2). i didn't touch point 3 (marking firefox < 77 as partial) because i wasn't sure it fits the partial_implementation guideline, happy to add it if you think it should be.

entry.title: integrity-violation report: style destination behind Firefox pref
entry.content:
Firefox supports style in Integrity-Policy blocked-destinations behind the security.integrity_policy.stylesheet.enabled pref in https://bugzilla.mozilla.org/show_bug.cgi?id=1974247. Since the integrity-violation report type shipped in Firefox 149, these violations are reported with "style" as the body.destination.

This adds api.ReportingObserver.ReportingObserver.options_parameter.types_property.integrity-violation.destination_style, with Firefox 149 behind the pref, so the IntegrityViolationReport page can list "style" as a destination and show that no browser supports it by default.

Claude states this, but I have not verified it:

  • Firefox: dom/security/IntegrityPolicyService.cpp maps DestinationType::Style to "style" in the report body, and dom/security/IntegrityPolicy.cpp only adds Style when the pref is set. The pref is still false in main.
  • Chrome: false. services/network/public/cpp/integrity_policy_parser.cc only accepts script.
  • Safari: false. WebKit's Source/WebCore/loader/IntegrityPolicy.cpp hard-codes "script" as the report destination.

Related docs work can be tracked in mdn/content#46592

entry.title: Add srcdoc, data: and blob: subfeatures to iframe loading
entry.content:
Summary

Adds blob_url, data_url and srcdoc subfeatures to html.elements.iframe.loading, as proposed in #30950. The spec runs the lazy loading steps for srcdoc and for every URL scheme, but Chromium only lazy-loads http(s) URLs, and WebKit doesn't lazy-load blob: URLs.

The names follow webdriver.bidi.network.getData.data_url. I left the new keys untagged, so the loading-lazy web feature keeps its Baseline status until the web-features maintainers decide how to map them.

Test results and supporting details

npm test passes.

Manual test: a page with four loading="lazy" iframes 30,000 px below the viewport (same-origin http, srcdoc, data: and blob:). It records which iframes load before the window load event and which still haven't loaded 3 seconds later.

http(s) srcdoc data: blob:
Chrome 157 lazy loads at once loads at once loads at once
Safari 26.4 lazy lazy lazy loads at once

Firefox isn't installed here, so its data comes from the sources below.

Sources:

  • Chromium, false: IsFrameLazyLoadable() returns false for anything but http(s) URLs (html_frame_owner_element.cc). The open bug (crbug.com/40703417) only names srcdoc, so impl_url is only on that row.
  • Firefox 121: iframe lazy loading shipped in 121, when dom.iframe_lazy_loading.enabled became true by default (StaticPrefList.yaml at FIREFOX_121_0_RELEASE, nightly only in 120). Firefox's WPT expectations at that tag have no iframe-loading-lazy.html.ini (meta directory), so all five subtests, including the srcdoc, data: and blob: ones, were expected to pass. Those subtests have been in WPT since July 2020 (web-platform-tests/wpt@37281cb).
  • Safari 16.4 for srcdoc and data:, false for blob:: WebKit stopped restricting iframe lazy loading to http(s) URLs in July 2022 (252852@main, bug 243225), before iframe lazy loading shipped in 16.4, the parent's version. WebKit's expected results for the WPT haven't changed since that commit: srcdoc and data: pass, and blob: fails (iframe-loading-lazy-expected.txt). The manual test on Safari 26.4 matches.

Related issues

Fixes #30950

entry.title: Add `options.type` parameter to PerformanceObserver.observe()
entry.content:
Summary

Adds api.PerformanceObserver.observe.options_type_parameter. The method shipped with entryTypes only, and observe({ type: "..." }) came later, so the current data (Safari 11, Chrome 52, Firefox 57) overstates support for code that uses type.

I named it options_type_parameter instead of type_parameter, following the guideline for properties of parameter objects (same as options_capture_parameter on addEventListener()).

Test results and supporting details

Versions follow what @caugner found in #24584, and I checked each one against the source:

  • Chrome 74: "[PerformanceObserver] Ship |type| in PerformanceObserverInit" (e80ce141047415c1412c5c300f5ff206e45aa8b7), first in 74.0.3690.0 per chromiumdash.
  • Firefox 68: bug 1539006, target milestone mozilla68.
  • Safari 14: WebKit d37ab8ceef1841fad029605443a7177f805299fd (bug 209216), WebKit 610.1.24. Safari 13.1 is 609.1.20 and Safari 14 is 610.1.28.
  • Node.js 16.0.0: lib/perf_hooks.js in v15.14.0 only reads entryTypes; lib/internal/perf/observe.js in v16.0.0 reads type (nodejs/node#37136).
  • Deno 2.7: the first PerformanceObserver in ext/web/15_performance.js (denoland/deno#31875) already handles type, so same as the parent.
  • Bun 1.0.22: src/bun.js/bindings/webcore/PerformanceObserver.cpp at bun-v1.0.22 already handles init.type, so same as the parent.

observe({ type: "mark" }) delivers entries in Node 22 and Bun 1.3.11. npm run lint on the file passes and lint:fix makes no changes.

Related issues

Fixes #24584

entry.title: Mark kernelUnitLength on feConvolveMatrix and feDiffuseLighting as deprecated
entry.content:
Summary

The Filter Effects spec says kernelUnitLength is deprecated on <feConvolveMatrix> and <feDiffuseLighting>, so this sets deprecated: true on those two attribute entries.

Test results and supporting details

Both attribute definitions in the current Filter Effects draft end with this note:

This attribute is deprecated and will be removed. It does not provide a reliable way to create platform independent results. Future versions of this specification will cover this use case.

See https://drafts.csswg.org/filter-effects/#element-attrdef-feconvolvematrix-kernelunitlength and the feDiffuseLighting definition right below it in the same spec.

I left svg.elements.feSpecularLighting.kernelUnitLength as it is, since its definition doesn't have that note. If you'd rather keep all three consistent, I'm happy to add it here.

Lint passes locally.

Related issues

Fixes #28178
